# Managing State

State lets a component remember information between renders. When you call `setCount`, the component renders again with the **new** value.

![A diagram of the render cycle](/images/render-cycle.png)

<Diagram name="render-cycle" />

## Choosing the state structure

Keep the state as small as you can. You can read more in the [state guide](/learn/state).

- Group related state together
  - Avoid _redundant_ state
  - Avoid duplicated state
- Avoid deeply nested state

1. Install the helper package:

   ```sh
   npm install tiny-state
   ```

| Principle | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Group | `position` |

```js
const [count, setCount] = useState(0)
```
